title: An everywhere-defined graded Proj immersion detects relative ampleness
statement: Let $h:Z\to S$ be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and let $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}\mathcal A_d$ be a quasi-coherent graded commutative $\mathcal O_S$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra, def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures]. It need not be generated in degree one and $\mathcal A_0$ need not equal $\mathcal O_S$. Suppose $\psi:h^*\mathcal A\to\bigoplus_{d\ge0}L^{\otimes d}$ is a graded algebra homomorphism [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $U(\psi)$ be the union, over $d\ge1$, of the open loci on which $\psi_d:h^*\mathcal A_d\to L^{\otimes d}$ is surjective, and let $r_{L,\psi}:U(\psi)\to\operatorname{Proj}_S(\mathcal A)$ be the canonical morphism [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map, def-nagata-relative-proj]. If $U(\psi)=Z$ and $r_{L,\psi}$ is an immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], then $L|_{h^{-1}(V)}$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] for every affine open $V\subseteq S$.

steps.text: Fix an affine open $V\subseteq S$, put $T=h^{-1}(V)$, and write $A=\mathcal A(V)$ and $P=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$. The affine restriction of the relative Proj and of the canonical map in [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map] identifies $r_{L,\psi}|_T$ with the ordinary canonical morphism $r:T\to P$ attached to the graded ring map $A\to\Gamma_*(T,L|_T)$ induced by $\psi$. Because $U(\psi)=Z$, the positive-degree images generate $L|_T$ at every point, so the nonvanishing opens of positive-degree homogeneous sections cover $T$.

The morphism $r:T\to P$ is an immersion and $T$ is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-trf-qc-immersion-proj-open-factor] to obtain a quasi-compact open subscheme $Y\subseteq P$ and a factorization $T\xrightarrow{i}Y\xrightarrow{u}P$ with $i$ a closed immersion and $u$ the open inclusion.

By [lem-trf-proj-qc-open-twist-ample], there is an integer $e\geq1$ for which $\mathcal O_Y(e)$ is invertible and ample. Restricting this ample module along the closed immersion $i$ and using [lem-trf-ample-restrict-closed-immersion] shows that $i^*\mathcal O_Y(e)$ is ample on $T$. Via $u^*\mathcal O_P(e)=\mathcal O_Y(e)$, this is ampleness of $r^*\mathcal O_P(e)$.

The ring map and canonical morphism from Step 1 satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-trf-proj-canonical-map-twist-comparison], so for some $d\geq1$ there is an isomorphism $r^*\mathcal O_P(dk)\simeq L|_T^{\otimes dk}$ for every $k\geq1$. Taking $k=e$ and combining the usual tensor-power identification $\mathcal O_P(e)^{\otimes d}\simeq\mathcal O_P(ed)$ with Step 3 gives that $L|_T^{\otimes ed}$ is ample, using [lem-sc-ample-positive-tensor-power] for the $d$th power of the ample module $r^*\mathcal O_P(e)$.

Since $ed>0$, every affine nonvanishing section cover for the positive tensor power $L|_T^{\otimes ed}$ is also a cover by sections of positive tensor powers of $L|_T$ (with the same nonvanishing loci). Thus $L|_T$ is ample directly from [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. As this holds for the inverse image of every affine open $V\subseteq S$, the asserted relative ampleness follows from the quasi-compactness of $h$.
